chunks_canon.text: This methodology sets out how the capital requirement for unexpected losses is determined for each exposure.
It applies to all exposures of the lending book. Trading positions are outside its scope.
The probability of default (PD) is the likelihood that an obligor defaults within one year.
The loss given default (LGD) is the share of the exposure that is lost when the obligor defaults.
The exposure at default (EAD) is the amount outstanding when the obligor defaults.
The requirement uses the normal distribution function N and its inverse, where ρ denotes the asset correlation.

The probability of default is estimated from internal ratings and is reviewed every year.
The probability of default is never taken below 0.03%.
The floor applies before any other step of the calculation.
The conditional probability of default is evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor.

The asset correlation falls with the probability of default: R = 0.12 * (1 - exp(-50 * PD)) / (1 - exp(-50)) + 0.24 * (1 - (1 - exp(-50 * PD)) / (1 - exp(-50))).
The correlation therefore lies between 0.12 and 0.24.
The loss given default is at least the floor of its segment, as set out in Table 3.

The unexpected loss rate is the conditional probability of default less the probability of default: UL = PDc - PD.
K is the product of LGD and UL.

model_units.text:
#' Capital requirement per unit of exposure
#'
#' The product of the loss given default, floored by segment, and the unexpected loss rate.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param lgd loss given default
#' @param segment segment of the exposure: Retail, Corporate or Bank
#' @export
capital_k <- function(pd, lgd, segment) {
  check_inputs(pd, lgd)
  lgd_f <- pmax(lgd, lgd_floors[lgd_floors$segment == segment, "lgd_floor"])
  pdc <- cond_pd(floor_pd(pd), asset_correlation(pd))
  ul <- pdc - pd
  lgd_f * ul
}

#' Risk-weighted amount
#'
#' The requirement scaled by 12.5 and multiplied by the exposure at default.
#' @param k capital requirement per unit of exposure
#' @param ead exposure at default
#' @export
rwa <- function(k, ead) {
  k * 12.5 * ead
}

#' Effective maturity

#' At least 1 year and capped at 5 years.

effective_maturity <- function(m) {

}

#' Asset correlation
#'
#' The asset correlation falls with the probability of default and lies between 0.12 and 0.24.
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @export
asset_correlation <- function(pd) {
  w <- (1 - exp(-50 * pd)) / (1 - exp(-50))
  0.13 * w + 0.24 * (1 - w)
}

model_units.name: cond_pd

formulas.linear: pdc = normal_cdf((normal_inverse(pd) + sqrt(rho) * normal_inverse(0.999)) / sqrt(1 - rho))

model_units.text:
#' Conditional probability of default
#'
#' Evaluated at the 99.9th percentile of the systematic factor:
#' \deqn{PDc = \Phi\left(\frac{\Phi^{-1}(PD) + \sqrt{\rho} \cdot \Phi^{-1}(0.999)}{\sqrt{1 - \rho}}\right)}
#' @param pd probability of default
#' @param rho_a asset correlation
#' @param q confidence level, defaults to 0.999
#' @export
cond_pd <- function(pd, rho, q = 0.999) {
  a <- qnorm(pd)
  b <- sqrt(rho) * qnorm(q)
  pnorm((a - b) / sqrt(1 - rho))
}
